sections.label: Women's Charter amendment purposes
sections.summary: The proposed Women's Charter amendments cover six areas: supporting younger couples, protecting children in divorce, spousal maintenance for incapacitated husbands, voiding marriages of convenience, supporting family violence victims, and online vice enforcement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: Specifically, the proposed amendments to the Women's Charter will, firstly, help support younger couples in their transition into married life and parenthood; secondly, better protect the interest of children affected by their parents' divorce; thirdly, allow incapacitated husbands and ex-husbands to apply for spousal maintenance when there is a clear need; fourthly, void marriages of convenience; fifthly, better support vulnerable persons in family violence and crisis situations; and lastly, strengthen law enforcement against online vice.

sections.label: Marriage dissolution cohort statistics
sections.summary: 20.3% of the 1998 marriage cohort had dissolved before the 15th anniversary, compared to 12.3% of the 1987 cohort.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: To cite a statistic, for example, 20.3% of our 1998 marriage cohort had dissolved before the 15th anniversary, compared to 12.3% of the 1987 marriage cohort.

sections.label: Extending Marriage Preparation Programme
sections.summary: Over 95% found the programme useful, so the Women's Charter rules will be amended to extend the Marriage Preparation Programme to all marriages where one party is a minor.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: We are very heartened that over 95% of them found it useful.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: We will now amend the Women's Charter rules to extend the Marriage Preparation Programme to all marriages where one party is a minor.

sections.label: Mandatory parenting programme before divorce
sections.summary: A new section 94A will require divorcing couples with minor children who cannot agree on all divorce matters to attend a mandatory parenting programme before filing for divorce, starting with those having a child below 14.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: Social workers, counsellors and lawyers have told us it is much better to have divorcing parents consider their children's well-being early, before the divorce process formally starts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: We are, therefore, introducing a new section 94A in the Women's Charter to require divorcing couples with minor children who are not able to agree on all matters of divorces to attend a mandatory parenting programme (MPP) before they can file for divorce.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: For a start, those with at least one child aged below 14 will be required to attend the programme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: We plan to eventually extend this requirement to those with children aged below 21.

sections.label: Funding and running pre-divorce programme
sections.summary: The pre-divorce mandatory parenting programme will be funded by the Ministry and conducted by Divorce Support Specialist Agencies, which have served over 3,000 divorcing couples since starting a year ago.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: The pre-divorce MPP will be funded by my Ministry and conducted by the Divorce Support Specialist Agencies (DSSAs).

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: Since they started operating a year ago, they have served over 3,000 divorcing couples.

sections.label: No gender neutrality on maintenance
sections.summary: After discussions, the conclusion is that society is not fully ready for gender neutrality on spousal maintenance, and the Women's Charter will not be renamed a Family Charter at this time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: After extensive discussions with stakeholders and internal deliberations, we have concluded that, our society is not quite fully ready for gender neutrality on the spousal maintenance front and we will not rename the Women's Charter as a Family Charter at this time, despite some calls to do so, in line with the philosophy of gender-neutrality.

sections.label: Spousal maintenance for husbands
sections.summary: Amendments will allow spousal maintenance to be extended to husbands and ex-husbands for the first time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: He is very bitter because he has no recourse for support, despite years of having provided for his wife and family.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: We are proposing amendments that will allow, for the first time, spousal maintenance to be extended to such husbands and ex-husbands.

sections.label: Conditions for a man's claim
sections.summary: Only a man incapacitated before or during marriage, unable to earn a livelihood and unable to support himself can claim maintenance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: Only a man who is: one, incapacitated before or during the course of the marriage; two, unable to earn a livelihood and three, unable to support himself, therefore, can claim maintenance.

sections.label: Two groups of defaulters
sections.summary: There are two groups of defaulters, those who cannot pay and those who won't pay, and financial assistance will be extended to vulnerable wives and children where the husband genuinely cannot pay.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: We find that there are basically two broad groups of defaulters: firstly, those who "cannot pay"; secondly, those who "won't pay".

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: We will extend timely financial assistance to vulnerable wives and ex-wives and their children in cases where the husband or ex-husband genuinely cannot pay maintenance.

sections.label: Appointing a Maintenance Record Officer
sections.summary: Working closely with the Courts, a Maintenance Record Officer will be appointed to stop husbands who refuse to pay maintenance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: They know their husbands refuse to pay maintenance for themselves and their children, and we intend to seriously stop such irresponsible behaviour.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: So, we are working closely with the Courts to appoint a Maintenance Record Officer (MRO).

sections.label: Doubling supervised exchange capacity
sections.summary: By July this year, the Divorce Support Agencies will double their capacity of supervised exchange and visits for children.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: By July this year, the Divorce Support Agencies will double their capacity of supervised exchange and visits for children.

sections.label: Singaporean and non-resident marriages
sections.summary: The number of marriages between Singaporeans and non-residents increased from 5,411 in 2004 to 6,686 in 2014.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: The number of marriages between Singaporeans and non-residents has been Page: 40 increasing from 5,411 in 2004, to 6,686 in 2014 a decade later.

sections.label: Convicted parties count 2015
sections.summary: As of 2015, 218 parties have been convicted.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: As of 2015, 218 parties have been convicted.

sections.label: Amendments on online vice
sections.summary: The amendments make it an offence to operate websites offering sexual services for payment and let Police act against those who aid prostitution for gratification.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: The proposed amendments will enhance the Police's levers to address online vice.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: They will make it an offence for persons in Singapore to operate or maintain in Singapore any website or other remote communication service that offers or facilitates the provision of sexual services in return for payment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: They will also enable the Police to take action against a person who aids or will aid the prostitution of another person by providing any service, such as setting up a website to advertise such services, and who receives any gratification, whether cash or in kind, for providing that service.

sections.label: Consultation feedback and amendments
sections.summary: Others gave inputs during consultation, and the proposed amendments and other changes aim to strengthen marriages, support families and protect the vulnerable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: Others have given their inputs and feedback during our consultation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: I believe that this set of amendments we are proposing, and the other changes we are making to policies and services will help strengthen marriages, support families and render protection and assistance to those who are more vulnerable.

sections.label: Women's employment and alimony
sections.summary: Women's employment rate was 76% for ages 25 to 54, and men still cannot claim alimony apart from a small group in genuine need.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Labour force statistics last year showed that employment rate for women in Singapore was 76% for the prime working ages of 25 to 54.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: According to some divorce lawyers, between 30% and 50% of women in divorce cases earn as much, if not more than the men.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: This is in line with alimony laws in societies where gender equality is actively pursued, such as Britain, the United States and Canada.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: But the Ministry deduced from talks with various groups that our society is not ready for women to shoulder the same responsibilities as men, and so, up till today, men are still not able to claim alimony, apart from a small group of men in genuine need that can get spousal support.

sections.label: Courts weighing wife's means
sections.summary: The Courts should weigh carefully cases where the wife is better off, referring to Justice Choo Han Teck's 2014 rejection of a $120,000 claim.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I also believe that the Courts should weigh carefully in cases where the wife is better off than the husband, and has not been financially dependent on him during their marriage.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I refer to the case where Justice Choo Han Teck, who, in 2014, generated somewhat of a debate when he rejected a woman's $120,000 maintenance claim from her former spouse after their 10-year marriage ended in 2012.

sections.label: MPP for divorcing parents
sections.summary: Children in divorce are most vulnerable to negative emotions and negligence, and the speaker supports the Bill's implementation of an MPP for divorcing parents.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In a divorce, children are most vulnerable to negative emotions and negligence.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I support the Bill's implementation of an MPP for divorcing parents.

sections.label: Ex-husbands unable to work
sections.summary: Ex-husbands who cannot work due to health reasons will be able to seek maintenance from their ex-wife.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: First, those ex-husbands who cannot work due to health reasons will be able to seek maintenance from their ex-wife.

sections.label: Mandatory parenting programmes for divorcing parents
sections.summary: Divorcing parents must attend specialised parenting programmes to minimise divorce's impact on children, while many women face unpaid maintenance.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Second, we will make it mandatory for divorcing parents to attend specialised parenting programmes to minimise the impact of divorce on their children.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: On the other hand, there are still many women who face the problem of their ex-husband not-paying maintenance.

sections.label: Maintenance complaint application process
sections.summary: An aggrieved party must apply in person at the Family Courts for a maintenance complaint, and persistent defaults may exhaust her into giving up.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: For instance, where there is a default in the payment of the maintenance order, the aggrieved party has to make an application in person at the Family Courts to make a maintenance complaint and the Court will then serve a maintenance summons on the defaulter.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: However, sometimes in the case of persistent serial defaulters, the aggrieved party may be so tired out by the process of having to physically attend Court each time the defaulter defaults, that she eventually gives up claiming the maintenance amount due to her.

sections.label: Making maintenance complaint applications convenient
sections.summary: The speaker urges making maintenance complaint applications more convenient, allowing family service centres, proxies for incapacitated husbands, and bailiffs or the MRO to enforce arrests.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: As such, while I listen with interest what the Minister has shared with regard to the appointment of an MRO, I would like to urge further the following considerations.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: That, one, the application process for maintenance complaints to be made more convenient for an ex-husband or ex-wife who wants to serve a private summons on their ex-spouse who has defaulted on maintenance payments.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: An example could be to have the application done at family service centres and in the case of an incapacitated husband, that a proxy should be allowed.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: And in the case where there is a warrant of arrest issued for an ex-spouse who can pay and refuses to pay, that an agency or system of bailiffs and perhaps the MRO that the Minister has spoken about, be tasked to enforce the actual arrest of the defaulter to give teeth to the charter.

sections.label: Children affected by divorce in 2014
sections.summary: In 2014, 5,172 and 1,689 children below 18 were affected by divorce under the Women's Charter and AMLA respectively, and school counsellors could assist.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The numbers of children below the age of 18 who were affected by the divorce of their parents in 2014 were 5,172 and 1,689 for marriages under the Women's Charter and the Administration of Muslim Law Act respectively.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Can school counsellors be roped in to assist and work with social workers of MSF to better help these children?

sections.label: Register for vulnerable children from divorces
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether MSF can set up a register to track vulnerable children from divorces and assist disadvantaged ones long-term.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Page: 46 Is it possible for MSF to set up a register to keep track of vulnerable children from divorces and to assist these children, especially the more disadvantaged ones, on a long-term basis?

sections.label: Divorce and annulment numbers
sections.summary: Divorces numbered 1,551 in 1980 and 6,861 in 2014, or 7,307 including annulments.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The absolute numbers of divorces were 1,551 in 1980 and 6,861 in 2014, or 7,307 including annulments.

sections.label: Marriage and parenting courses
sections.summary: The speaker suggests pre-marriage courses plus three subsequent marriage courses in communication, conflict resolution and marriage enhancements, and parenting courses for minors.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: This will strengthen marriages more before they deteriorate or start to breakup.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Thus, I am suggesting not just giving pre-marriage courses but three further subsequent marriage courses in communication, conflict resolution and marriage enhancements together with parenting courses for minors.

sections.label: Preventive measures for marriages
sections.summary: The question asks whether MSF will explore further preventive measures at the beginning when marriage requirements are considered.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Will MSF explore further preventive measures at the very beginning when requirements for marriages are being considered?

sections.label: Registrars investigating marriage applications
sections.summary: The question asks whether registrars of marriages can be given authority to investigate marriage applications and refuse certificates for fraudulent marriages.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Can our registrars of marriages be given the authority to investigate and form opinions on whether the marriage applications are genuine and perhaps to refuse issuance of certificates for fraudulent marriages?

sections.label: Embassies publicising marriage information
sections.summary: The suggestion is that embassies in these nationals' countries publicise this information and discourage them from using this route to gain permanent residency.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Maybe our embassies in the countries of these nationals should publicise this information and help to discourage them from using this route to gain permanent residency in Singapore.

sections.label: Bill on divorce and violence
sections.summary: The Bill lets Courts order divorcing parents to attend the MPP, restates who can apply for protection orders, and makes incapacitated ex-husbands eligible for maintenance from ex-wives.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The Bill gives the Courts powers to order divorcing parents to attend the MPP and restates who can apply for a protection order in situations of family violence.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The second set follows the principle of gender equality and makes incapacitated ex-husbands eligible for receiving maintenance from their ex-wives.

sections.label: 2011 Charter amendments enforcement orders
sections.summary: The 2011 Charter amendments on financial counselling, community service, earnings attachment and credit bureau recovery only dented the problem, with maintenance enforcement applications falling from 1,900 in 2009 to 1,700 in 2013.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The 2011 amendments to the Charter giving the Courts powers to impose financial counselling, community service, attachment of earnings and credit bureau recovery have only managed to cause a dent in the problem.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: It has been reported that the number of applications for enforcement orders on maintenance had only dropped from 1,900 in 2009 to 1,700 in 2013.

sections.label: Central agency recovering maintenance
sections.summary: The Government can help vulnerable divorcee families protect children's interests by setting up a central agency with strong powers to recover maintenance for them.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The Government can help tremendously vulnerable divorcee families to protect the interest of the children by setting up a central agency with strong enforcement powers to recover maintenance on behalf of the families.

sections.label: Commissioner powers for unwed parents
sections.summary: The Charter could give the Commissioner for the Maintenance of Families powers to proactively help single unwed parents, especially mothers, claim child maintenance from the biological father.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The Charter could also give the Commissioner for the Maintenance of Families powers to take a proactive approach in helping single unwed parents, especially the mothers, to claim child maintenance from the biological father.

sections.label: Enforcing child support reduces pregnancies
sections.summary: Studies show enforcing child support for single unwed mothers, coupled with widespread education and publicity, can reduce non-marital pregnancy rates, addressing moral hazard worries.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Page: 49 If the worry is that helping single unwed parents will cause the moral hazard of promoting more children born out of wedlock, then the Government should know that studies have shown that enforcing child support for single unwed mothers, when coupled with widespread education and publicity, can reduce the rate of non-marital pregnancies.

sections.label: Expanding persons applying for PPOs
sections.summary: People often experience helplessness and cannot act to protect themselves and their families, so the range of persons empowered to apply for PPOs needs expanding.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: They often experience helplessness and cannot act to protect themselves and their families.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: We need to expand the range of persons empowered to apply for PPOs.

sections.label: Police empowered to apply protection orders
sections.summary: As in many overseas jurisdictions, the Police, whom social workers, doctors, victims and children of victims trust, should be empowered to apply for protection orders.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Last, and definitely not least, like in many jurisdictions overseas, the Police, to whom social workers, doctors, victims and children of victims turn to as the trusted investigative and enforcement agency, should be empowered to apply for protection orders.

sections.label: Removing Part XI from Women's Charter
sections.summary: The speaker says Part XI conflates prostitution and sexual exploitation with the family and should be removed and integrated into other legislation.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In fact, Part XI is an anomaly and its inclusion in the Charter conflates prostitution and sexual exploitation with the family.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I believe this Part is best taken out and its provisions integrated with the Prevention of Human Trafficking Act and the Penal Code.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Once Part XI is removed, and the principles of parental responsibility and gender equality are re-affirmed, future revisions of the Women's Charter will provide us with the opportunity to do something progressive and leading the times, shaping society for the better, like what the original Charter did in 1961.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: There have been calls for the Women's Charter and all other pieces of legislation dealing with the family, including the Children and Young Persons Act, to be combined into a landmark piece called the Family Charter.

sections.label: Proposals for families and Family Charter
sections.summary: The passage lists proposals including treating children as stakeholders, a central maintenance agency, child support for unwed mothers, tackling family violence, and consolidating legislation as the Family Charter.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Treat children as stakeholders in the divorcing process, set up a central agency to help single-parent families collect maintenance, help single unwed mothers obtain child support to reduce poverty and out-of-wedlock pregnancies, tackle family violence by Page: 51 empowering the Police and persons who can help the victims to apply for protection orders, allow all ex-husbands to apply for maintenance and let the Courts decide on gender-neutral grounds, and consolidate the pieces of legislation as the Family Charter to establish a firm foundation for families to thrive into the 21st century.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The year 2021 will mark the 60th year of the enactment of the Charter.

sections.label: Maintenance for incapacitated ex-husbands
sections.summary: The speaker supports in principle a provision allowing specifically incapacitated men who cannot work to apply for maintenance from ex-wives, while raising concerns for MSF.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: In this case, inserting a provision to allow men, very specifically incapacitated men who cannot work and support themselves, to apply for maintenance from their ex-wives is a step in the right direction.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: While we need to take bold steps and to recognise that the society has indeed, progressed and evolved and that there is greater gender equality that we observe now in our society, and that, with that, I support the provisions in principle, I do have a few concerns that I hope MSF can address.

sections.label: Strengthening maintenance implementation for ex-wives
sections.summary: The speaker urges MSF to strengthen implementation and support for ex-wives who need but have not received their monthly maintenance.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: While the provision is a step in the right direction, I do urge MSF to continue to strengthen its implementation and support to the ex-wives who need but have yet to receive their monthly maintenance.

sections.label: Maintenance from irresponsible person who impregnated
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether MSF would consider requiring maintenance from the irresponsible person who may have impregnated a woman, making her a single unwed mother.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Fourthly, I would like to ask whether MSF would consider putting in requirements to demand for maintenance from the irresponsible person who may have impregnated a woman, resulting in her becoming a single and unwed mother.

sections.label: Children's interests in divorce via MPP
sections.summary: The speaker notes children usually have no say in separation yet deal with the pain, and is encouraged that MSF is trying to better protect children affected by divorce through the MPP.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: In a separation, children usually have no say in the Page: 53 decision and yet they are compelled to deal with the pain.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Therefore, I am encouraged to hear that MSF is trying to better protect the interest of children affected by their parents' divorce through the MPP.

sections.label: MSF service scaling plans
sections.summary: A question asks whether MSF will scale up such a service and has other plans to complement it.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: In this respect, could MSF share whether such a service will be scaled up and whether MSF has other plans to complement such an effort?

sections.label: Supporting genuine foreign-spouse marriages
sections.summary: Marriages of convenience cannot be tolerated, but more must be done to recognise and support genuine marriages with foreign spouses.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: While a marriage of convenience cannot be tolerated nor condoned, as it violates the sacredness of marriage, we must do more to recognise and support genuine marriages with foreign spouses.

sections.label: Flats near parents for couples
sections.summary: Couples could be allowed or facilitated to get flats in mature estates near their parents for parental and familial support.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: For instance, we can try to allow or facilitate couples getting access to flats in mature estates near their parents so that they can have parental and familial support when they eventually have children.

sections.label: Five key areas of Bill
sections.summary: The Bill's proposed amendments focus on five key areas, including child interests, maintenance, protection, voiding marriages of convenience and remote sexual services.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: The proposed amendments in the Bill are largely focused on five key areas: (a) taking care of the child/children's interests through the MPP for divorcing parents; (b) maintenance for incapacitated men; (c) enhanced protection for women and professionals at places of safety; (d) voiding marriages of convenience; and (e) remote communications facilitating provision of sexual services.

sections.label: Divorce filings and children
sections.summary: Between 2005 and 2009, divorces averaged 6,025 at the Family Court and 1,780 at the Syariah Court, with many involving children.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Between 2005 and 2009, an average of 6,025 divorces was filed at the Family Court and 1,780 at the Syariah Court.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: It was stated that half of the Family Court's and 70% of the Syariah Court's cases involved families with children and these figures continue to climb.

sections.label: Compulsory programme before divorce
sections.summary: Current law requires mediation and counselling after a divorce writ is filed, but the amendment makes attendance compulsory before filing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Our current law requires parents with children under 21 years of age to attend mediation and counselling after a divorce writ is filed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: But the proposed amendment makes it compulsory to attend the programme before filing for divorce; this is welcome.

sections.label: Women's Charter and section 46
sections.summary: The Women's Charter empowers Singapore women, and this amendment lays to rest the anomaly of section 46 on mutual cooperation and equal rights in the matrimonial household.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: The Women's Charter is about empowering our Singapore women, and their financial standing has grown in tandem with their contributions to our nation, from bread-makers in the kitchen to breadwinners in this generation for their families.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: This amendment also finally lays to rest the anomaly of section 46 of the same Charter, which states that husband and wife are both "mutually bound to cooperate with each other in safeguarding the interests of the union and in caring and providing for the children" and under section 46(4), "have equal rights in the running of the matrimonial household".

sections.label: Maintenance for incapacitated ex-husbands
sections.summary: The speaker says maintenance payments to incapacitated ex-husbands must be in order if the wife earns more, and asks for the number of such ex-husbands.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Therefore, in all fairness, if the wife is earning more, maintenance payments to incapacitated ex-husbands must be in order.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: I would, however, like to know if the Ministry could share, if available, the number or estimated number of incapacitated ex-husbands in Singapore who would benefit from this proposed amendment.

sections.label: Violence against women survey
sections.summary: A 2013 International Violence Against Women Survey in Singapore found 9.2% of 2,006 female respondents reported at least one incidence of violence by a man since age 16.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: With regard to enhanced protection for women and professionals at places of safety, according to a 2013 report on the International Violence Against Women Survey conducted in Singapore, the prevalence of violence against women in Singapore shows that nearly one in 10 of the 2,006 female respondents surveyed, or 9.2%, reported having experienced at least one incidence of violence by a man in their adult lifetime since the age of 16.

sections.label: Number of convictions declined
sections.summary: The number of those convicted went down from 284 in 2013 to 170 in 2014.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: The number of those convicted has gone down – from 284 in 2013 to 170 in 2014.

sections.label: Matchmakers and overseas sexual service sites
sections.summary: The speaker says more proactive action is needed to ensure matchmakers bringing foreign brides are bona fide, and seeks clarification on how the Ministry will deal with overseas sites under new section 146.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Agreed, it will void the marriage of convenience.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: But more proactive action is perhaps required by the respective agencies in ensuring that the matchmakers involved in bringing over foreign brides are bona fide and are not mere pimps in disguise, masquerading as arrangers of marriages of convenience.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: With regard to remote communication, facilitating provision of sexual services under the new section 146, I would like to seek clarification from the Minister on how the Ministry will deal with sites that are located overseas.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: A simple Google search will reveal that there are many such sites but there are no provisions under section 146 for this.

sections.label: Bipartisan support for the Bill
sections.summary: The Bill has bipartisan support, and the speaker says it is timely to amend the Charter so it protects women, their families and marriages.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: This is one Bill that has brought bipartisan support from across different parties.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: It is therefore incumbent upon us to honour and treasure this Charter and it is timely that we make the necessary amendments so that it protects not only women but their families, and marriages, too.

sections.label: Mandatory parenting programme before divorce
sections.summary: The passage supports a proposed section 94A requiring an MPP for appropriate parties before divorce proceedings, with exemptions provided.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: Parents are encouraged to resolve the issues on custody, care and control and access as early as possible.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: I am pleased to see further developments in the form of the proposed amendments to the Women's Charter, in particular the addition of the new section 94A to prescribe an MPP for appropriate parties before the commencement of divorce proceedings.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: I believe that the introduction of an MPP will be useful to remind parents of the impact of divorce on their children and the need to prioritise their children's interests in their decisions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: I note that in the proposed section 94A, provisions are made for exemptions from MPP.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: This is clearly necessary as such programmes may not be relevant for divorcing parties who do not have children and there is also some room for the Court to make appropriate orders in certain circumstances, for example, when a case needs to be expedited where there is domestic violence.

sections.label: Family support programmes for disputing families
sections.summary: The passage supports empowering the Court to direct parties or their children to attend family support programmes and activities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: Familial relationships cannot be terminated and family members who are in dispute need processes which help to repair their relationships.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: I, therefore, support the proposal to empower the Court to also direct parties or their children to attend family support programmes and activities in appropriate circumstances.

sections.label: Maintenance for incapacitated husbands
sections.summary: The passage addresses proposed amendments to sections 69 and 113 of the Women's Charter extending maintenance to an incapacitated husband or former husband.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: I would, lastly, like to touch on the proposed amendments to sections 69 and 113 of the Women's Charter.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: These amendments relate to the extension of maintenance to an incapacitated husband or former husband, a point which has been raised by fellow Members of this House.

sections.label: Calibrated maintenance for incapacitated husbands
sections.summary: The passage appreciates changes limited to incapacitated husbands but urges caution on allowing husbands to claim maintenance from wives.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: So, post-divorce, such women are financially usually more vulnerable.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: I, therefore, appreciate that the proposed changes are calibrated, nuanced and limited to incapacitated husbands.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: It is important that we move towards addressing gaps in the law, addressing the grievances for these husbands who may have difficulties in maintaining themselves.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: However, I think it is important to be cautious of any further move to allow husbands to claim maintenance from their wives, at this juncture.

sections.label: Support for proposed Bill changes
sections.summary: The passage welcomes and supports the proposals in the Bill, describing most proposed changes as dynamic and in tandem with societal developments.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: I am, therefore, grateful and heartened that most of the proposed changes are dynamic and in tandem with societal developments.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: I welcome and support the proposals in this Bill.

sections.label: MPP before filing for divorce
sections.summary: The passage states that section 94A mandates divorcing couples with children who cannot agree on all divorce matters to attend an MPP before filing.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Section 94A mandates that divorcing couples with children who cannot agree on all matters of divorce will need to attend an MPP before they can file for divorce.

sections.label: Spousal maintenance for incapacitated husbands
sections.summary: Sections 69 and 113 let incapacitated husbands or ex-husbands claim spousal maintenance from wives or ex-wives if unable to work.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: The amendment proposed in sections 69 and 113 of the Bill is to allow incapacitated husbands or ex-husbands to claim spousal maintenance from their wife or ex-wives if they are incapacitated during the marriage to the extent that he is unable to work to support himself and at the time of the application for the maintenance is heard.

sections.label: Spousal abuse most common family violence
sections.summary: A 2013 PAVE study found spousal abuse victims made up 72% of all new family violence cases in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Based on a study done by PAVE in 2013, the most common form of family violence in Singapore is spousal abuse victims and these victims, who are physically or psychologically abused by their spouses made up 72% of all new cases.

sections.label: Protecting identities of vulnerable women and girls
sections.summary: Sections 177A and 153 protect identities of vulnerable women, girls and protection work persons, and prohibit publishing shelter locations.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: By last year, the figure had more than tripled to 3,200." Recognising the realities and the increasing use of social media, the amendments made in sections 177A and 153 seek to protect the identity of vulnerable women and girls and persons in Page: 62 protection work and, hence, ensuring their safety.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Section 177A also prohibits the publication or broadcast of any information in the mass and social media that would reveal or is likely to identify the location of the shelter or residential facility or their residents.

sections.label: Extending publication prohibition to online media
sections.summary: Section 153 is amended to extend the prohibition on publishing identifying information to online media and social media.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Section 153 is also amended to extend prohibition on the publishing of information which may lead to the identification of women and girls in certain in-camera Court proceedings to also include online media and social media.

sections.label: Female labour force participation rate rise
sections.summary: The female labour force participation rate rose from 51.3% in 2004 to 58.6% in 2014.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: While we see greater participation in the workforce, and the numbers have been very encouraging especially in the last few years, the female labour force participation rate rose significantly from 51.3% in 2004 to 58.6% in 2014.

sections.label: Balanced amendments to Women's Charter
sections.summary: The Bill's amendments are balanced, recognising the spirit of the Women's Charter while addressing changing realities in society and the family.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: The amendments proposed in this Bill are balanced and seek to recognise the spirit of the Women's Charter while addressing the changing realities in society and the family.

sections.label: Spousal support for incapacitated men
sections.summary: The amendments will allow incapacitated men to seek spousal support from their ex-wives.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: With the latest amendments, I find it encouraging and progressive that, amongst other things, the proposed amendments will include allowing incapacitated men to seek spousal support from their ex-wives.

sections.label: Family responsibilities and workforce participation
sections.summary: In 2014, 10,200 male Singaporeans and PRs cited family responsibilities as the main reason for not working, and women's labour force participation rose more than men's since 2011.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: In 2014, 10,200 male Singaporeans and Permanent Residents cited "family responsibilities", such as childcare, caregiving to family members and housework, as the main reason for not working.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: One thousand and six hundred of them cited childcare as the main reason for being out of the workforce − more than double the number in 2006.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: In parallel, the labour force participation rate since 2011 increased more for women from 55% to 60%, versus men from 75% to 77%.

sections.label: Mandatory parenting programme before divorce
sections.summary: New section 94A implements MSF's proposal that parties with children must complete an MPP before filing for divorce if they have not agreed on divorce and all ancillary matters.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The new section 94A implements MSF's proposal that parties with children must complete an MPP before they can file for divorce, if they have not agreed on divorce and all ancillary matters.

sections.label: Domestic violence waiver and male maintenance
sections.summary: The speaker says the law should explicitly state no parenting programme is needed in domestic violence cases, and notes the Bill makes spousal maintenance available to incapacitated men.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Although the proposed section 94A(4) allows the Court's discretion in waiving the requirement of MPP, in my view, the law should explicitly and clearly state that no parenting programme needs to be attended in cases of domestic violence, rather than leaving the question up to the discretion of the judge.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The Bill amends the Charter so that spousal maintenance is available to men, but only where they have been incapacitated and are unable to support themselves.

sections.label: Proposed amendments and clarifications sought
sections.summary: The speaker proposes amending section 94A for domestic violence, questions section 160's detention of girls aged 16 to 21, and seeks clarity on PPOs, shelters and void marriages.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: First, amend the new section 94A to explicitly state that in situations of domestic violence, judges should not require divorcing parties to attend an MPP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Third, section 160 allowing the Director of Social Welfare to detain girls aged between 16 and 21 is extremely vague, broad and open-ended.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Fourth, I note the extension of the PPO regime to married under-21s and would like to raise the question whether these people will now be able to access shelters and "place of safety" if they become victims of domestic violence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Fifth, I recommend that all individuals under 21, not just those who have been married, can apply for PPOs on their own behalf.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Sixth, I seek more clarity as to the process by which a marriage can be found void and whether a decision of such gravity will be subject to judicial process.

sections.label: Support for marriage preparation programme
sections.summary: Members supported mandating the marriage preparation programme for minor couples.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: Members have given their support to mandate the marriage preparation programme for minor couples.

sections.label: Child-centricity and mandatory divorce parenting programme
sections.summary: The speaker agrees with two members on child-centricity and says this is why the Women's Charter is being amended to require parents contemplating divorce to attend MPP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: Ms Rahayu Mahzam and Ms Jessica Tan spoke on the importance of child-centricity, and I really could not agree more.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: This is why we want to amend the Women's Charter to require parents contemplating divorce to attend MPP.

sections.label: MPP programme results since 2015
sections.summary: Since the programme started in 2015, close to 150 children and their parents have benefited, with about 96% reporting reduced stress.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: Since the programme started in 2015, close to 150 children and their parents have benefited.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: The overwhelming majority – of about 96% reported a reduction in stress.

sections.label: What the MPP will include
sections.summary: The MPP will cover financial challenges, housing and living arrangements in divorce, child custody and access, and a joint workable parenting plan.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: The MPP will include a couple of things: to make sure that there are considerations on financial challenges involved; housing and living arrangements in a divorce; child custody and child access; and joint agreement on a workable parenting plan.

sections.label: Gender equality and not rushing pace
sections.summary: Her sentiments echoed an October Straits Times commentary titled 'A Reality Check in Gender Equality', and the speaker believes it is best not to rush and force the pace.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: Her sentiments echoed a The Straits Times commentary in October last year which was titled "A Reality Check in Gender Equality".

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: They are gradually shifting towards greater gender neutrality, but we believe, at this stage, it is best to not rush and force the pace.

sections.label: Extending maintenance to incapacitated men
sections.summary: The proposal to extend maintenance only to incapacitated men is a calibrated measure, though it may be reviewed in future.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: To sum up, while we may review this in future, the proposal to extend maintenance only to incapacitated men is a calibrated measure.

sections.label: Courts MRO for non-payment
sections.summary: Repeated court visits due to a vindictive ex-spouse not paying are agonising, so the MRO will be introduced in the Courts later this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: It is very agonising for an individual to repeatedly go to the Courts because the ex-spouse vindictively does not want to pay up.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: This is why the way we want to approach this is to set in place to introduce in the Courts the MRO which would take place later this year.

sections.label: Void marriages of convenience
sections.summary: Marriages are void only when a party is successfully charged and deemed guilty under section 57C of the Immigration Act for a marriage of convenience.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: Marriages are void only when at least one party is successfully charged and deemed guilty by the Courts under section 57C of the Immigration Act for entering into a marriage of convenience.

sections.label: Admission to place of safety
sections.summary: A girl is admitted to a place of safety only if the Director is satisfied it is in her best interests.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: A girl will only be admitted to a place of safety if the Director is satisfied it will be in her best interests, for example, if it is unsafe for the girl to remain with her immediate family or if she may engage in morally risky behaviours.

sections.label: Crisis shelter safety and disturbances
sections.summary: Crisis shelters are secured with CCTV cameras, with no serious breaches but two disturbances known to MSF in recent years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: For the safety of their residents, crisis shelters are housed in secured premises with closed-circuit television cameras.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: Thus far, there have been no serious breaches.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: There were two instances of disturbances at the shelters known to MSF in the last couple of years.

sections.label: Support programmes and MRO approach
sections.summary: Support programmes are not mandatory now; the MRO with the Family Justice Courts is the planned approach, with a tribunal as one possibility.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: At this moment, we do not envisage making it mandatory but what we do want to make sure is that the support programmes are in place for those who do need the support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: For adult couples, we encourage them to come forward.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: We are not at that stage where we plan to make it mandatory for non-minor couples.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: With regard to the tribunal, that is one possibility.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: But we believe that the approach that we plan to take in terms of putting in the MRO, working with the Family Justice Courts, would be one way to address this issue.

sections.label: Using MRO for expeditious processes
sections.summary: The MRO will be used to work the processes to make them as expeditious as possible.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: What we intend to do is to use the MRO to work the processes to make sure that it is as expeditious as possible.

sections.label: No register for divorce-affected children
sections.summary: There are no immediate plans to put all children affected by divorce on a register, though tracking vulnerable individuals is being looked at.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: So, I hear the Member's point that it is not just all children who are affected by divorce.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: We do not have plans at this point in time to put all these children on a register.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: I take the Member's perspective on whether this is something we should track.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: We are looking at the possibility of tracking individuals who are affected in different ways, not just by divorce but vulnerable in a different sense, because there is a long social tail of issues that can happen if the support is not provided and, indeed, whether some of these interventions should be brought to bear even if the individuals do not come forward.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: That is something that we are looking at but, at the present time, there are no immediate plans to put them on the register.

sections.label: Court-directed MRO investigation
sections.summary: The Court would direct the MRO to investigate and find out the background of individuals, especially those able to pay.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: Basically, the MRO would be directed by the Court to investigate and to find out the background to the individuals concerned, especially in cases where they are able to pay.
